items.title: USN-9115-1: Mini-XML vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that Mini-XML used unbounded recursion when deleting and writing XML nodes. An attacker could possibly use these issues to cause Mini-XML to crash, resulting in a denial of service. These issues only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS.

items.title: USN-9130-1: zutils vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that zcat in zutils incorrectly handled the -v option, leading to a buffer overflow. If a user were tricked into opening a specially crafted compressed file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9129-1: ZBar vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that ZBar incorrectly handled certain QR codes, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. If a user or automated system were tricked into scanning a specially crafted QR code, an attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information or execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9128-1: YADIFA vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that YADIFA did not check for infinite pointer loops when parsing DNS packets. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause YADIFA to consume excessive CPU resources, leading to a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9127-1: Syntastic vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Syntastic searched the current directory and its parents for checker configuration files. If a user were tricked into checking a file in a directory controlled by an attacker, the attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9126-1: tmpreaper vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that tmpreaper incorrectly handled certain mount operations, leading to a race condition. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to create arbitrary files, leading to privilege escalation.

items.title: USN-9124-1: RenderDoc vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that RenderDoc did not properly verify array sizes when serialising strings, leading to an integer overflow. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a buffer overflow, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9123-1: mechanize vulnerability
items.summary: Erik Krogh Kristensen and Rasmus Petersen discovered that mechanize used an inefficient regular expression to parse authentication headers. A malicious server could possibly use this issue to cause mechanize to consume excessive resources, leading to a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9122-1: pysha3 vulnerability
items.summary: Nicky Mouha discovered that pysha3 incorrectly handled certain SHA-3 operations, leading to an integer overflow. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause pysha3 to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9111-1: Mojolicious vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that the secure_compare function in Mojolicious did not run in constant time when comparing strings of different lengths. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to determine the length of a secret string.

items.title: USN-9109-1: Apache::Session::Browseable vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Apache::Session::Browseable did not verify the certificates of remote LDAP servers by default. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform a machine-in-the-middle attack and obtain sensitive information.

items.title: USN-9107-1: joblib vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that joblib evaluated the pre_dispatch parameter of the Parallel class as Python code. If an application passed untrusted input to this parameter, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9105-1: Apache Jackrabbit vulnerability
items.summary: Lukas Reschke discovered that the WebDAV support in Apache Jackrabbit incorrectly checked the content type of requests when protecting against cross-site request forgery. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform cross-site request forgery attacks.

items.title: USN-9103-1: HTMLDOC vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that HTMLDOC incorrectly handled certain malformed URIs. If a user or automated system were tricked into opening a specially crafted HTML file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause HTMLDOC to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9101-1: Apache Groovy vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that Apache Groovy incorrectly handled the deserialization of MethodClosure objects. An attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service. (CVE-2015-3253) It was discovered that Apache Groovy incorrectly handled serialization mechanisms.

items.title: USN-9099-1: Eterm vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Eterm incorrectly handled certain escape sequences. An attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code if a user displayed specially crafted text in the terminal.

items.title: USN-9098-1: DokuWiki vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that DokuWiki did not properly encode the call parameter of AJAX requests. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform a reflected file download attack and trick a user into running arbitrary programs.
